description: NEW: LA inscription incised on the outside walls of a clay basket (large kanistros with two vertical handles) from the east room of the Anemospilia sanctuary; incomplete but 'of particular importance'; nothing legible on the profile drawing fig. 388 per Olivier
publication: Sakellarakis & Sapouna-Sakellaraki 1997, ibid., vol. I, 333 and vol. II, 422-423
pages: vol. I p. 333, vol. II pp. 422-423; rapport p. 189
notes: No reading printed; NOT mentioned again in Rapports 2001-2021; ABSENT from silver - genuine enumeration gap, no reading available from the rapport series

description: Conoid-pyramidal seal ('amulette') from the LM cemetery tholos tomb, cf. Rapport 1991-1995 p. 423; republished with photo and drawing of the inscription; Papadopoulou continues to call it an amulet
publication: Papadopoulou 1997, in Driessen & Farnoux (eds) La Crete mycenienne (BCH Suppl. 30), 335, fig. 23
notes: ABSENT from silver; Younger (round-1 channel) flags it as likely not an inscription at all; BCH Suppl. on Persee is open

description: Clay disc, surface find, pierced with suspension hole and cut; three rather similar signs of which one, two or all three could be A 344 (possibly related to AB 131); announced Rapport 1991-1995 p. 427, now published
publication: Schoep 1998, A Note on the Inscribed Material of the 1994 Excavations, in MacGillivray, Sackett & Driessen, Excavations at Palaikastro 1994 and 1996, BSA 93, 264-268, pl. 50
notes: Sign identifications tentative (A 344 x1-3); ABSENT from silver - genuine gap; not mentioned again in later rapports

description: Pithos fragment engraved before firing, LM IB; three signs read ]AB 188-54-28[ (all three dotted/uncertain)
publication: Floyd 1995, Fragments from Two Pithoi with Linear A Inscriptions from Pseira, Kadmos 34, 39-48
notes: ABSENT from silver (silver has only PS Za 2 / PSI Za 1 for Pseira-Psychro) - genuine gap WITH a (dotted) published reading in hand via this rapport; a_ingestible candidate

description: Second pithos fragment engraved before firing, LM IB; a single fragmentary sign
publication: Floyd 1995, ibid.
notes: ABSENT from silver - gap (single fragmentary sign, no usable reading)

description: 'Selon la rumeur' a vase fragment with the remains of three or four signs; Olivier hopes it will be published under the designation ZA Zb 35 proposed here
publication: Unpublished rumor
notes: RENAMED: Rapport 2001-2005 p. 208 declares the Austin announcement erroneous and renames the item ZA Zb 39 (still inedit there); never published through 2021; ABSENT from silver - 26+ years pending

description: Fragments of at least two clay tablets (maximum six), found 1992 in space Delta 18a in a lekane together with a sealing; logograms A 302 and/or A 303 (two agricultural products), A 306 (probably OVIS f) and A 54+09 (TELA+SE), the last with at least 200 units; in adjacent Delta 18b ~67 clay sealings of Cretan clay from Cretan seals, some 'look-alikes' of Haghia Triada and Sklavokampos sealings, some with traces of organic ties on the back (lost perishable documents)
publication: Boulotis 1998, ibid., 407-410; logogram photo Doumas PAA 1993 [1996] pl. 113 fig. c
notes: RESOLVED LATER: became THE 7-12 (six fragments) in Rapport 2001-2005/2006-2010 with Boulotis 2008 preliminary publication; silver carries ad-hoc IDs THEfr.1-3 + THEtab.4-5 whose identity with THE 7-12 is UNVERIFIED - identity flag

description: Owens's Corpus of Published Inscriptions in Linear A (COPILA): catalogue of LA inscriptions published, 'rediscovered' or announced after GORILA; classification errors noted (e.g. MO Zg 1 for Zf 1); its 'rediscovered' items = five pseudo-inscriptions on Knossos architectural supports + one incised mark on a Mycenae bronze basin (rejected); its value = the three forgotten documents above
publication: Owens 2005, Corpus of Published Inscriptions in Linear A (COPILA), DO-SO-MO 6, 26-45
notes: BOOKKEEPING row (resource, not an item); pseudo-inscriptions and the Mycenae basin mark explicitly NOT admitted

description: INEDIT: clay 'token' ca. 2 cm diameter, <1 cm thick, six signs running along the edge, tops outward, forming an almost complete circle; found in a Second-Palace-period building; support without parallels, hence the Wy prefix; Olivier (autopsy, pers. comm.) reads AB 08-01[ ]02-27-27 (hapax) despite sign-form idiosyncrasies; the long vertical stroke between 08 and 27 = numeral 1 or a divider; circular-layout parallels: HT Wc 3010/3015, SY Za 1, PK Za 15, KN Zc 6/7, KN Zf 31, KN Zf 13 (spiral)
publication: To be published by G. Rethemiotakis (never appeared in Rapports 2006-2021)
notes: ABSENT from silver - genuine gap; Olivier's provisional reading printed in rapport but NO editio princeps through 2021; Younger lists it (round-1 channel)

description: NEW (numbering fix): flat-based nodule HM 676 with traces of inscription, datable MM II; mentioned by Hallager as Wb 55 (Minoan Roundel II 225, 295 - numbering to be rejected: the Wa 53/54 of Minoan Roundel are anepigraphic) and as Wb 53 (Floreant p. 285); absent from Olivier's rapports; here numbered PH Wb 53
publication: Hallager 1996, Minoan Roundel II, 225, 295; Hallager 1999 in Floreant, 285
notes: DELETED LATER: autopsy (Rapport 2006-2010) shows plant-ligament traces, not writing; inscription suppressed, number 53 kept vacant (Rapport 2011-2015); silver correctly LACKS PHWb53 - absence is the endorsed state

description: Inscription of three or four signs incised on a vase fragment; 'announced erroneously in the Austin rapport as Zb 35'; still inedit
publication: Unpublished
notes: ABSENT from silver - never published through 2021 (not mentioned in Rapports 2006-2021); genuine pending item since 1996-2000

description: Two ANEPIGRAPHIC roundels bearing on the rim the hieroglyphic seal impressions #135 and #136 (CMS V Suppl. 1B (1993) nos. 326 and 325), not yet classed among the anepigraphic roundels; assigned inscription-numbers under the 'paradoxical but inevitable' practice (fn. 44)
publication: CMS V Suppl. 1B (1993) nos. 325-326; cf. Rapport 1991-1995 pp. 420-421
notes: BOOKKEEPING row - anepigraphic, NOT corpus candidates; matters only for the SA We 3 renumbering

description: Nodulus, ex We 1 (= CHIC #137), renumbered because of {SA Wc 1}/{SA Wc 2}; Olivier initially read (left to right) an arithmogram, a klasmatogram and an isolated syllabogram; after autopsy: the arithmogram is a simple control mark, and the inscription = the sinistroverse sequence of AB 04 and klasmatogram A 708 (K), or alternatively a ligature of the two ('04'+'708'), proposed as new sign A 505bis; A 708 is exclusive to LA
publication: CMS V Suppl. 1B (1993); cf. Rapport 1991-1995 pp. 420-421, 430; Minoan Roundel II 218
notes: ABSENT from silver (only SAMWa1 present for Samothrace) - genuine gap WITH reading in hand; a_ingestible candidate; MM II-III

description: Nodulus found 1999, published by Matsas as We 2 (CMS V Suppl. 3 (2004) no. 343); same findspot and layer as {SA Wc 1}/{SA Wc 2}/We 3, MM II-III; one side bears a seal impression (possibly hieroglyphic, cf. rapport CH section 1.2.2.1); the other an inscription engraved with a stylus; Matsas: ligature A 609 or new ligature AB 08 + A 303 followed by numeral 1 or 10; Olivier (autopsy): ligature AB 08+04 (08 dotted), proposed as new sign A 506bis; the lower-left dot is a stylus perforation from applying a control mark, not a numeral; both signs also exist in CH so the LA attribution is not fully certain, but the exclusive-LA klasmatogram A 708 on twin nodulus We 3 reinforces it
publication: Matsas 2004, CMS V Suppl. 3, no. 343 (as SA We 2)
notes: ABSENT from silver - genuine gap WITH reading in hand; a_ingestible candidate; designation collision Matsas We 2 vs Olivier/Del Freo We 4; round-1 row (from Rapport 2016-2021 fn. 14-15) superseded by this fuller record

description: NUMBERING NOTE: the rapport fixes the Thera list as Zb 1-4, Zg 5, Zb 6 (House of the Ladies, inedit), THE 7-12 (6 [?] tablet fragments, Delta 18a, 1993, inedits), Zb 13 (Xeste 2 pithos); it REJECTS Karnava's scheme (Michailidou's Room Delta-3 amphora fragment - signs 'ne semblent pas constituer une veritable inscription' - as Zb 6, shifting old 6-9 to 7-10, Xeste 2 = Zb 11); Michailidou's proposed readings for that fragment: A 318-AB 08 / 41 / 27 (all dotted)
publication: Michailidou 2000-2001 [2002], Indications of Literacy in Bronze Age Thera, Minos 35-36, 12-15; Karnava in Horizon (2008), 378
notes: BOOKKEEPING/DIVERGENCE row: silver Thera IDs are a MIXED BAG (THEZb5 AND THEZg5; THEZb6 AND THEZb7; ad-hoc THEfr.1-3/THEtab.4-5; Del Freo's Zb13 + editors' Zb15) - divergence-register candidate

description: NEGATIVE: Zurbach re-studied the spindle-whorls published by Schliemann 1875, in which Godart had recognized two LA inscriptions; probable dating Troy II or III and comparison with contemporary whorls identify the engraved signs as decorative motifs of a local tradition; same conclusion for vases Schmidt 2444 and 2445
publication: Zurbach 2003, Schriftahnliche Zeichen und Topferzeichen in Troia, Studia Troica 13, 115-116
notes: NEGATIVE VERDICT row - not LA; correctly absent from silver

description: NEGATIVE: cylindrical alabastron with four signs engraved after firing, three compatible with LA (Egetmeyer: first ~ A 706, second ~ A 339, fourth ~ A 304; third without parallels); origin unknown, stylistically East-Mediterranean/Cypriot, LH IIIA2 - early IIIC; signs could have been added elsewhere/later; a forgery cannot be excluded; DEL FREO: leave this graffito OUT of the LA corpus
publication: Egetmeyer & Zavadil 2004, Ein Spatbronzezeitliches Alabastron aus dem ostlichen Mittelmeerraum mit Graffito, Kadmos 43, 151-158
notes: NEGATIVE VERDICT row - excluded from corpus; correctly absent from silver

description: NEW: signs incised on two LM I vase fragments detected summer 2007 during pottery study of the Block C houses, including 'a sign for olive oil' (Kentro Newsletter); to be published together with a third subsequently identified fragment in the excavation report for that part of the settlement (Brogan pers. comm.)
publication: Kentro. The Newsletter of the INSTAP Study Center for East Crete 10 (Winter 2007-2008), 3
notes: ABSENT from silver (no designations assigned); NOT resolved in Rapports 2011-2021; corpus/bronze/kentro_newsletters holds the source newsletter; Younger lists Mochlos pointers (round-1 channel)

description: NEGATIVE x2: Civitillo reviews the incised Pelikata sherds (Faure 1989: LA) concluding - like Driessen 1990 (Rapport 1986-1990 p. 446) - that they are NOT writing; the same conclusion for the Haghios Athanasios 'tablet' (Kontorli-Papadopoulou, Papadopoulos & Owens, Kadmos 44 (2005) 183-186: 'A possible linear sign from Ithaki (AB 09 SE)?')
publication: Civitillo 2008-2009, Sulle presunte 'iscrizioni' in lineare A e B da Itaca, AION N.S. 15-16, 71-87
notes: NEGATIVE VERDICT row - not writing; correctly absent from silver

description: PUBLISHED (preliminary, photos only - no facsimiles or transnumerations; definitive edition announced as imminent): six badly-fired tablet fragments recomposed from smaller ones (~30 tiny fragments remain unplaced), found August 1993 inside an asaminthos (bathtub) in the SW corner of room Delta 18a, Complex Delta; LM IA; possibly 2-3 original tablets at most; partial readings printed: THE 7 (opisthographic) face a last two lines = traces of a sign + numeral 7, then logogram AB 21f + numeral 46, face b numeral traces (maybe 40); THE 8 = a sign interpreted as ligature AB 54+09 (if correct, new sign A 534bis) + numeral 200[; THE 10 = isolated AB 67; THE 11 and 12 = traces maybe compatible with logogram A 302; THE 9 has no logograms (not discussed)
publication: Boulotis 2008, ibid., 67-94
notes: ABSENT from silver under THE 7-12; silver's ad-hoc THEfr.1-3 + THEtab.4-5 (five items for six fragments) are UNVERIFIED candidates for these - identity flag; definitive edition still pending through 2021

description: NEGATIVE-LEANING: Negri proposes to recognize an LA inscription (PER Zg 1) in the two signs incised on two contiguous blocks of the left jamb of Tholos 1; the signs are indeed comparable with AB 04 and AB 08, but (as Negri concedes) they may be two simple mason's marks placed side by side by chance; GORILA's decision not to include the Peristeria signs 'semble donc irreprochable'; if included at all the prefix should be Ze (stone architectural support), not Zg (fn. 62)
publication: Negri 2001-2002, Un'iscrizione L.A 'dimenticata': PER Zg 1, in Graeco-Latina Brunensia (Festschrift Bartonek), 175-177
notes: Correctly absent from silver (GORILA exclusion endorsed)

description: STATUS: during study of pottery from the recent excavations new fragments with isolated LA signs, all incised before firing, have been identified (Zurbach pers. comm.); the final publication will reorganize the epigraphic material and slightly modify the Rapport 2001-2005 numbering
publication: Zurbach pers. comm.
notes: BOOKKEEPING row; the reorganization happened: Niemeier, Del Freo & Zurbach 2015, Kadmos 54 (see Rapport 2011-2015 row)

site: Haghia Triada (Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Firenze)
description: REPUBLICATION without modifications of the nine Haghia Triada nodules with LA marks kept in Florence (already in GORILA II and CMS II 6, nos. 340-346); Jasink 2009, catalogue CR 226-CR 233
publication: Jasink 2009, La collezione di sigilli e cretule egee, in Jasink & Bombardieri (eds) Le collezioni egee del Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Firenze, 77-88, tab. 40-44
notes: BOOKKEEPING row; items already in corpus via GORILA II

description: DELETED: the direct examination of the flat-based nodule HM 676 (Del Freo & Zurbach, Herakleion Museum, July 2009) EXCLUDES that the visible grooves are traces of writing - they are probably traces of simple plant ligaments (suggestion E. Fiandra per litteras 2009-08-11); 'L'inscription est donc supprimee'; the number 53 should not be reused for other documents
publication: Autopsy result reported in this rapport
notes: REMOVAL row (the item Del Freo himself had added in Rapport 2001-2005): silver correctly LACKS PHWb53; number kept vacant - hence PH 54 for the next Phaistos item (Rapport 2011-2015)

description: NEW: roundel (12.183, diam. ca. 2 cm) from the same context as GO 2; two seal impressions on the rim countermarked by a vertical stroke; one or more signs incised on one face; Younger: inscription traced to the RIGHT of the impressions (unusual - normally below) comprising a NEW LOGOGRAM (a circle with two superposed dots inside) followed by numerals 2 and 20 (perhaps relating to the two impressions); Del Freo alternative: a ligature of AB 80 (cf. PK 1.7) with another sign - perhaps AB 74, or AB 85 (Olivier)
publication: Younger in Watrous et al. 2015, ibid., 446-448, fig. 33
notes: ABSENT from silver - genuine gap; reading disputed (new logogram + '2' '20' vs AB 80-ligature)

description: NEW FIND REPORT: stone libation table with incised signs, found August 2013 in a niche inside a bench; inverted-pyramid shape, surface stepped on three levels, cavity on top (Warren form 2B / Muhly form A.V; inscribed parallels KN Za 10, PK Za 8, perhaps PK Za 16, per Davis 2014, 68-70, 340, 347, 357); per the first information from E. Sapouna-Sakellaraki, the twelve 'steps' carry twelve incised signs 'some of which' would be in LA
publication: Zominthos Project field notes 2013 week 5; To Vima 2013-08-11; Chronique des fouilles en ligne ID 4430; cf. Sapouna-Sakellaraki 2015, Prakt, 282-283 (round-1 row)
notes: CORRECTLY ABSENT: Rapport 2016-2021 judges an LA inscription 'tres improbable' (masons' marks matching Hood 2020 types; round-1 row EXCLUDE-unless-overturned) and the table is absent from silver; ROUND-1 AMBIGUITY RESOLVED: silver's ZO1 is a DIFFERENT object (vase logogram *409+VS with numeral 217, tablet-like record - earlier Sakellarakis-excavation find, identity/source to verify), NOT this table; Younger's ZO Za 1 = this table
